articles.title: 4 WWE stars who disrespected Nikki Bella with John Cena relationship remarks
articles.summary: WWE News: A major chapter in WWE Hall of Famer Nikki Bella's life was her relationship with John Cena. The duo was together for a long time. However, they parte.
articles.body: A major chapter in WWE Hall of Famer Nikki Bella's life was her relationship with John Cena. The duo was together for a long time. However, they parted ways in 2018 because their beliefs and life goals didn't align. Over the years, multiple superstars have taken huge jabs at Bella in that context. However, these four WWE stars really went over the line:4. AJ LeeAJ Lee was the reigning WWE Divas Champion in 2014 when the Bella Twins were getting all the hype due to their high-profile relationships and reality TV series, Total Divas. During a promo segment on RAW, Lee mocked both Nikki Bella and her sister by taking a jab regarding their boyfriends, John Cena and Daniel Bryan, respectively. She said, “It’s about time somebody breaks it to the Bellas, talent is not s*xually transmitted.”3. Ronda RouseyRonda Rousey had been on top of the women’s division for a year in WWE in 2018. The Bella Twins returned and, after a brief alliance, turned their back on the Rowdy One. During a heated promo exchange, Nikki said that she has broken more barriers and doors than Rousey. This led Rousey to retaliate and say: “The only door you knocked down was a door to John Cena’s bedroom. He eventually threw you out of that door.”2. Becky LynchBecky Lynch and Nikki Bella engaged in a rivalry following The Fearless One’s WWE comeback in 2025. A memorable in-ring segment saw both superstars trade heated words. The Man boasted that she and her husband, Seth Rollins, were WWE's top wrestling couple. Right then, Lynch said that at one point it was Nikki Bella and John Cena without mentioning his name. Moreover, Lynch ended the rant by saying that Bella could not see him anymore. Lynch said, “You can’t see him anymore.”1. Paige Nikki Bella began a feud with Paige after betraying her after their six-woman tag team matches at SummerSlam 2026. The two women met in a backstage segment on SmackDown ahead of their battle in Mexico City a week later. articles.title: El Betis puede soñar en grande
articles.standfirst: Su victoria ante el Lille lo sitúa en la terna de favoritos al 'top 8' para Versus
articles.summary: Su victoria ante el Lille lo sitúa en la terna de favoritos al 'top 8' para Versus
articles.body: El Real Betis vivió una noche inolvidable en su regreso a la Champions League 21 años después de su última participación. El conjunto de Manuel Pellegrini remontó un 0-1 inicial en el Stade Pierre-Mauroy para imponerse por 3-2 al Lille. Los franceses se adelantaron pronto por medio de Ayase Ueda, pero el Betis reaccionó con contundencia gracias al doblete de Marc Bartra y al tanto decisivo de Michael Parrott, completando así una remontada de gran mérito ante un rival que llegaba de finalizar tercero en la pasada Ligue 1. El triunfo en Francia se suma además a una racha muy sólida del conjunto verdiblanco en las últimas semanas, coronada por el histórico éxito conseguido días antes ante el Real Madrid en La Cartuja, resultado que ya disparó las alarmas en el liderato liguero blanco. Con este nuevo triunfo europeo, el Betis suma su primera gran alegría continental en más de dos décadas, una inyección de moral que llega justo antes de un calendario exigente, con la visita del Porto en la próxima jornada de la fase liga. Ese buen momento de forma se ha trasladado directamente al mercado de las casas de apuestas. Versus paga ya a una cuota de 3.75 que el Betis termine la fase liga entre los ocho primeros clasificados, posición que otorgaría el pase directo a octavos de final sin necesidad de disputar la ronda de play-off. Se trata de una cifra que, aunque todavía sitúa al conjunto andaluz como aspirante secundario frente a los grandes gigantes del continente, refleja la mejora de percepción que ha generado su victoria de prestigio ante un rival con experiencia reciente en la máxima competición europea. Más interesante resulta todavía el otro gran mercado que ofrece Versus para el conjunto verdiblanco. La cuota de que el Betis termine la fase liga entre el noveno y el vigésimo cuarto puesto, posiciones que permiten seguir con opciones de clasificación a través de la ronda de play-off. En este apartado, la casa de apuestas paga apenas 1.9, una cifra que confirma que el mercado considera altamente probable que el Betis, como mínimo, prolongue su presencia en la competición más allá de la fase liga, independientemente de si logra o no el billete directo a octavos. Con el liderato de LaLiga todavía como objetivo secundario tras su reciente triunfo ante el Real Madrid, y con este arranque perfecto en la Champions League, el Betis de Pellegrini vive una de las temporadas más ilusionantes de su historia reciente. La combinación de solidez defensiva, gol por parte de Bartra y el aporte de las nuevas incorporaciones como Parrott o el propio Fidalgo, invita a pensar que el conjunto verdiblanco puede seguir dando sorpresas en las próximas jornadas de la máxima competición continental.

articles.title: Browns Star Denzel Ward Joins Guardians Ownership Group
articles.summary: Cleveland Browns and former Ohio State star Denzel Ward has purchased a minority stake in the Cleveland Guardians.
articles.body: Denzel Ward has a mere uphill walk to check on his new investment. The Cleveland Browns star cornerback has purchased a minority stake in the Cleveland Guardians, the team announced on Wednesday morning. Ward is the second NFL player with a tie to the greater Cleveland area to purchase a minority stake in the team this year; Kansas City Chiefs tight end and four-time All-Pro Travis Kelce — who grew up in Cleveland Heights, Ohio, which is roughly 20 minutes east of Huntingon Bank Field, home of the Browns — bought a minority stake in the Guardians in May. Meanwhile, Ward is from Macedonia, Ohio, which is roughly 25 minutes south of Progressive Field, home of the Guardians. "Cleveland is my hometown. I’m so blessed to be able to show up for this city on the field and now as a part of the Guardians organization," Ward said in a statement, according to Cleveland.com. "I couldn’t be more grateful to the Dolan family and David Blitzer for the opportunity to continue to pour into this community and give back to the best fans in the world." Ward is expected to throw out the first pitch for the Guardians' Sept. 15 game against the Chicago White Sox. "Denzel Ward is a hometown hero on the field and off it," Guardians chairman and CEO Paul Dolan and vice chairman David Blitzer said in a joint statement. "His excellence, character and commitment to this community — including his work with the Make Them Know Your Name Foundation — make him a perfect fit for our organization. We are proud to welcome him as a partner in the Guardians' future." Last NFL season, Ward, a five-time Pro Bowler, totaled one interception, nine passes defended and 39 combined tackles across 15 regular-season games. Cleveland selected Ward, who has spent his entire eight-year NFL career with the Browns (2018-25), with the No. 4 pick in the 2018 NFL Draft out of Ohio State. Cleveland signed the 29-year-old Ward to a two-year, $62.2 million extension in July, with the $31.1 million average annual value putting him third among NFL cornerbacks. As for the team Ward is now a part-owner of, the Guardians (74-72) are in possession of the third American League wild-card seed, one game up on the Toronto Blue Jays for the last AL playoff spot and two games behind the White Sox for first place in the AL Central.

articles.title: Lions Star Jahmyr Gibbs: 'For Sure' Take Me With No. 1 Pick In Fantasy Football
articles.summary: Detroit Lions star running back Jahmyr Gibbs expressed that people should "for sure" take him with the No. 1 pick in fantasy football.
articles.body: Jahmyr Gibbs is the highest-paid running back in NFL history, and he thinks that should be reflected in your fantasy football draft. "For sure," Gibbs said with a reported smile Tuesday when asked if he'd take himself with the No. 1 pick in a fantasy football draft, according to the Lions' team website. "I'm either going to make a lot of people happy or mad." The Detroit Lions signed Gibbs, a Pro Bowler in each of his three seasons in the NFL (2023-25), to a three-year, $67.5 million extension in August, with the $22.5 million average annual value a record for a running back. Last season (2025), Gibbs rushed for 1,223 yards and 13 touchdowns on 5.0 yards per carry, while tallying 77 receptions for 616 yards and five touchdowns. The year prior (2024), he rushed for 1,412 yards and an NFL-high 16 scores on 5.6 yards per carry. Now, Gibbs, who has averaged 246.5 carries per season since 2024, is likely in store for a larger workload this season, as the Lions traded veteran running back David Montgomery, who averaged 187.3 carries per season from 2023-25, to the Houston Texans. Last season, Gibbs and Montgomery were the only Detroit players to get the call on the run more than three times, combining for 401 carries. Moreover, aside from Gibbs, the Lions' current running back room – Jacob Saylors and Sione Vaki – has a combined nine NFL carries under their belt. "I guess I'm getting most of the carries. I feel good [about that]," Gibbs expressed about likely getting more carries. "It's nothing I haven't done before. It's going to be cool." Following a 9-8 season that saw them miss the playoffs for the first time since 2022, the Lions fired offensive coordinator John Morton, who replaced the outgoing Ben Johnson – the now-head coach of the Chicago Bears. Former Arizona Cardinals offensive coordinator Drew Petzing is Detroit's new coordinator. After being fifth in the NFL in rushing yards in 2023 (135.9 per game) and sixth in 2024 (146.4 per game), the Lions were 14th (120.1 per game) last year. Gibbs and the Lions open the 2026 regular season at home against the New Orleans Saints on Sunday afternoon (1 p.m. ET on FOX).

articles.title: Carlos Alcaraz and Ben Shelton’s US Open night takes a shocking turn as Martina Navratilova reacts to 3:33 a.m. finish
articles.summary: International Sports News: Martina Navratilova has criticized the US Open schedule after Carlos Alcaraz and Ben Shelton’s quarterfinal started around 11 p.m. and finished at 3:3.
articles.body: Martina Navratilova has criticized the US Open schedule after Carlos Alcaraz and Ben Shelton’s quarterfinal started around 11 p.m. and finished at 3:33 a.m. on Tuesday night. The match became the latest finish in US Open history, according to the official US Open website. Navratilova reacted to the late start on X, saying the tournament needs to make changes because such timings are not normal for players.Martina Navratilova calls Carlos Alcaraz-Ben Shelton’s late US Open start “not OK”Martina Navratilova has criticized the US Open schedule after Carlos Alcaraz and Ben Shelton were forced to begin their quarterfinal after 11 p.m. on Tuesday night. The match then went deep into the early morning, finishing at 3:33 a.m. local time. The official US Open website confirmed that it was the latest finish in tournament history. Navratilova reacted on X while the scheduling delay was becoming clear.“Something has got to give… this is not ok and it is not normal … no other sport might start at 11 AM or 11 PM. In the same event…” Navratilova wrote on X.The delay came after a long day on Arthur Ashe Stadium. The schedule began at 11:30 a.m. with Aryna Sabalenka facing Linda Noskova. Frances Tiafoe and Alex Michelsen followed, and their match lasted four hours and 38 minutes. That pushed the later matches well behind their planned times.Jessica Pegula and Emma Navarro then played the first match of the night session. Their contest also went beyond two hours, which meant Alcaraz and Shelton did not get onto court until after 11 p.m. By then, the two players were facing a very different challenge from the one they would have faced with an earlier start.Navratilova’s complaint was aimed at the scheduling rather than either player. Her point was that the same event can begin matches in the morning and still have players starting another match around 11 p.m. The former world No. 1 has also spoken out about late-night tennis during this year’s tournament.Carlos Alcaraz and Ben Shelton finish latest US Open match at 3:33 a.m.Once the match finally started, neither Carlos Alcaraz nor Ben Shelton was able to finish the contest quickly. The quarterfinal lasted four hours and 28 minutes and went to a deciding-set tiebreak before Shelton pulled off one of the biggest wins of his career.The official US Open website reported that the No. 8 seed beat defending champion Alcaraz 6-7(5), 6-1, 6-3, 1-6, 7-6(7). Shelton ended the match with a 146-mph ace at 3:33 a.m., setting the tournament’s latest finishing time.The win also gave Shelton his first victory over a player ranked inside the world’s top three. He will now face fellow American Frances Tiafoe in Friday’s semifinal. Alcaraz, meanwhile, saw his US Open title defense come to an end after he had won his previous 18 Grand Slam matches.The late finish was especially striking because the match itself was so demanding. Shelton had to stay focused through five sets after waiting until late at night to begin, while Alcaraz also had to deal with the physical demands of a match that ended in the early hours of the morning.For Navratilova, that was the larger issue. Her message pointed to a scheduling system that can leave players waiting for hours before being asked to play a major match, with the final point sometimes coming close to sunrise.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Garrett Wilson: Jets Making Playoffs This Season 'Very Realistic'
articles.summary: New York Jets star wide receiver Garrett Wilson thinks making the playoffs this season is "very realistic."
articles.body: Garrett Wilson has high standards for the New York Jets this season. "[Making the playoffs is] very realistic," New York's star wide receiver said after stating that making the playoffs defines a successful season, according to ESPN. "I think it should happen. I'll say that. It's our job to go play ball and do it, but that's how I feel about it." The Jets are coming off a 3-14 season, haven't posted a winning season since 2015 and haven't made the playoffs since 2010, which is the longest drought in professional American sports. As for new faces, New York has two new coordinators, as head coach Aaron Glenn parted ways with offensive coordinator Tanner Engstrand after the 2025 season and moved on from defensive coordinator Steve Wilks in December of last season. Former Indianapolis Colts, Carolina Panthers and Stanford Cardinal head coach Frank Reich is the Jets' new offensive coordinator, while former Miami Dolphins and Detroit Lions defensive assistant Brian Duker is their new defensive coordinator; Duker was an assistant under Glenn when the latter was Detroit's defensive coordinator from 2021-23. On the personnel side, offensively, the Jets acquired veteran quarterback Geno Smith — who played the first four seasons of his career with the franchise (2013-16) — from the Las Vegas Raiders, signed guard Dylan Parham (two-year, $16 million deal), selected Oregon Ducks tight end Kenyon Sadiq with the No. 16 pick in the 2026 NFL Draft and traded up to select Indiana Hoosiers wide receiver Omar Cooper with the No. 30 pick. Defensively, New York selected Texas Tech Red Raiders defensive end David Bailey with the No. 2 pick in the draft, acquired safety Minkah Fitzpatrick from the Dolphins and signed linebacker Demario Davis (two-year, $22 million deal) — who also began his career with the Jets (2012-15 and 2017) — cornerback Nahshon Wright (one-year, $3.5 million deal) and defensive ends Joseph Ossai (three-year, $34.5 million deal), David Onyemata (one-year, $10.5 million deal) and Kingsley Enagbare (one-year, $9 million deal), among other moves. "Something is going to happen this year. I'm a faithful guy, and I believe that," Wilson, who also expressed that the team's struggles "weigh" on those who have been in the Hess colors for some time, said. "With the work we've been putting in, we have as good an opportunity as anybody in the league. I'm excited, man. We have a hell of a group here." Wilson, whom New York selected with the No. 10 pick in the 2022 NFL Draft out of Ohio State and signed to a four-year, $130 million extension in July 2025, was limited to seven games last season (2025) due to a knee injury, totaling 36 receptions for 395 yards and four touchdowns across the action he saw. Over the first three years of his career (2022-24), Wilson averaged 93.0 receptions for 1,083.0 receiving yards and 4.7 touchdowns per year, while never missing a game. Wilson and the Jets open the 2026 regular season on the road against the Tennessee Titans on Sunday afternoon. Of course, Tennessee's new head coach, Robert Saleh, was previously New York's head coach from 2021-24.

articles.title: Lewis Hall: Man United receive glimmer of hope in pursuit of Newcastle ace
articles.summary: 1Manchester United’s pursuit of Newcastle United left-back Lewis Hall ended in disappointment this summer. The Red Devils were looking for a long-term replac...
articles.body:
Manchester United's pursuit of Newcastle United left-back Lewis Hall ended in disappointment this summer. The Red Devils were looking for a long-term replacement for Luke Shaw and had identified the 21 year old as a priority target for the job.

Fast, technically gifted and blessed with an excellent passing range, Hall is a modern full-back who blends attacking desire with defensive discipline. His attributes make him a fantastic successor for Shaw at the Theatre of Dreams.

The 31 year old has entered the final year of his contract with United and the Red Devils wanted Hall to take his place. While the move failed to materialise, the English giants are expected to return for the player next summer.

However, a recent report relayed by The Peoples Person suggests that the young full-back is all set to sign a new deal at St. James' Park, raising doubts about a move to Old Trafford. While that has added to United's frustrations, a fresh update has now emerged from journalist Ben Jacobs that could be a shot in the arm for fans.

Speaking to talkSPORT , Jacobs said Hall is now tied to Newcastle United until 2031. He stated: "It's a five-year contract that adds two years to the existing deal. So it keeps Hall at the club until 2031. There were always these two extremes at play. Either Manchester United would make an approach, would have to overpay, and Hall would have been somewhat open to that move."

"Or he stays and under the new manager, Matthias Jaissle, is invested in the project, and then he signs a new deal. But it was never just going to continue with Hall staying and not being offered improved terms."

Jacobs insisted that Hall was not unsettled at St. James' Park, which has helped in the renewal process. He added: "Newcastle have been able to keep Hall because he was never unhappy with Newcastle the club, only unhappy with how last season ended, where he was in and out of the side."

"He lost his England place. Dan Burn , his Newcastle teammate, got picked in his place. All of that led Hall to, in the early part of the summer, at least put the brakes on signing because the nuts and bolts of this deal were in place in February or March."

"Then Eddie Howe leaves, Matthias Jaissle comes in. He's had a very positive effect on all players, including Lewis Hall. And Jaissle has told Hall he is integral, he is the number one left-back. Then from there, there was no hesitation in getting this deal over the line."

Jacobs went on to cite the example of Morgan Rogers to explain why a move cannot be entirely ruled out next summer. The English forward signed a new contract with Aston Villa in 2025, and joined Chelsea in a blockbuster transfer this summer.

Referring to that saga, Jacobs added: "Of course, we have to say with Morgan Rogers, he extended late last year. He still left the following summer."

"So I don't think we can say categorically, depending on how the season goes, that Hall is unavailable in the summer 2027 market. But it's a really positive sign for Newcastle. If everything now goes according to plan, then Hall will remain invested in this project."

Prising Hall away from Newcastle United has just become harder following his decision to sign a new deal. While United are likely to keep him under close watch, they could also consider alternative targets like Adrien Truffert .

✅ Ben Jacobs is a well-respected journalist.✅ The report ties in with a recent one saying Newcastle will still have to sell next summer.⚠️ It is pure speculation on Jacobs' part at the moment.

articles.title: Pair of NFL experts do not have Bengals making the playoffs
articles.summary: An ESPN writer and an NFL.com reporter have the Bengals on the outside of the playoffs again this year.
articles.body:
Kyle Brandt revealed his selections to make the AFC playoffs on Good Morning Football Tuesday morning. The Cincinnati Bengals were not among the teams he chose to make it to the playoffs.

After missing the playoffs for three straight seasons, it seems the Bengals still have a lot to prove when it comes to the media. Brandt selected the Baltimore Ravens to win the AFC North this season. A pick that going into this season is at least understandable.

The Ravens have won the AFC North two out of the last three seasons. The rushing attack returns Derrick Henry and Lamar Jackson . For a preseason prediction, there is at least nothing egregious about this one, even if it isn't the selection I would have personally made.

The more interesting selection came with his final wild card team. Brandt chose the Tennessee Titans to nab the final wild card spot for the AFC.

Robert Salah takes over as the head coach for the Titans, with Cam Ward entering his second season as the starting quarterback. While I do expect that defense to keep them competitive in a lot of games, I just don't think they have the offensive firepower to be a playoff team this year.

If we see the Titans make the playoffs over the Bengals something has gone seriously wrong. The Bengals added Dexter Lawrence , Jonathan Allen , Boye Mafe , Cashius Howell, and Bryan Cook as key contributors to a revamped defense. The entire starting offensive line returns for the first time in the Joe Burrow era. Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins are the best receiver tandem in the entire NFL.

Elsewhere, ESPN's Bill Barnwell's 2026 season predictions also do not have the Bengals making it back to the postseason. Barnwell has the Chiefs , Patriots , Ravens, and Texans winning their respective AFC divisions, while the Bills, Broncos , and Steelers of all teams get the Wild Card spots. He also has the Chiefs beating the Eagles to win the Super Bowl.

There are a lot of reasons to be optimistic as Bengals fans heading into the first game of the season on Sunday. It appears they will have to convince a lot of the media as the season goes.

Personally, I don't mind them being underdogs in the eyes of the talking heads around the league. The time is now, go out and show the world exactly who you are. It is time to make a run at winning the whole thing this season.

articles.title: World 100 Driver Rankings: Seeding The Entire 2026 Field
articles.summary: Ranking all 105 drivers in the 2026 World 100 field, from Eldora Speedway favorites Bobby Pierce and Jonathan Davenport to long-shot contenders.
articles.body:
The World 100 annually brings together Dirt Late Model racing's best to Eldora Speedway. If every driver arrived in Rossburg, Ohio, with a seed beside their name, how would the field stack up?

Ahead of Sept. 10-12's World 100, we're ranking every expected entrant based on current form, Eldora performance, event history and the subjective factors separating contenders from the rest.

These aren't cut-and-dried predictions of where each driver will finish, nor simply a ranking of the sport's best drivers. The question is more specific: Who enters World 100 weekend with the strongest case to outperform everyone seeded behind him at one of the sport's most demanding venues?

Each ranking includes the driver's hometown and a personalized outlook for World weekend along with previous credentials. From Eldora favorites to drivers chasing Saturday's feature, here's how we seed the 2026 World 100 field (seeding best-known entries as of Tuesday night):

Background: Capturing four of the last six Eldora crown jewels, including June's Dream, Pierce has supplanted Jonathan Davenport as the new favorite at the Big E. He did look vincible in last year's World 100, unable to fully overcome the invert while rallying from 27th to ninth. Amid another monstrous 27-win campaign, he'll try to become the first driver to capture five Eldora crown jewels in a seven-race span.

2. Jonathan Davenport (49), Blairsville, Ga.

Best World 100 finish: 1st (2015, '17, '19, '21, '22)

Background: Five-time World 100 winner remains gold standard at Eldora, finishing seventh or better in seven consecutive editions. He enters with 14 victories, including a dominant $50,000 triumph at half-mile Port Royal two weeks ago, but has gone winless in the last three Eldora crown jewels — and hasn't gone four straight without winning since the 2015 Dream. Another triumph would tie Billy Moyer for most World 100 victories and Scott Bloomquist for most overall Eldora crown jewels at 12.

3. Brandon Sheppard (1), New Berlin, Ill.

Background: The 17-time winner and Prairie Dirt Classic winner appeared capable of winning June's Dream before a right-front tire failure knocked him from second. He enters World week amid a season-long 14-race winless streak, however, and the World remains the glaring omission from his résumé, with sixth his best finish in 12 A-main starts. Still, his crown-jewel strength this season keeps him firmly in the top three.

4. Ricky Thornton Jr. (20RT), Chandler, Ariz.

Background: Thornton might not have cracked the top 10 a month ago, but he's peaking at the right time, since debuting a new car at the Topless 100. He's since produced his first three-race streak of top-two finishes since April 2025, highlighted by a dominant victory at half-mile Port Royal two weeks ago and 23 of 25 laps led in Sunday's Baltes Classic before a late slip-up. The defending World winner is also a perfect 7-for-7 in A-main attempts since his 2019 debut.

5. Dale McDowell (17M), Chickamauga, Ga.

Background: Perhaps nobody has been more dependable in the World than McDowell, whose 12 consecutive top-eight finishes include three straight podiums. He has gained 106 positions during that remarkable stretch, relentlessly contending regardless of where he starts. Twenty-one years after his breakthrough victory, the 60-year-old remains a legitimate threat to become the event's oldest winner.

Background: Emerging as one of Eldora's most reliable contenders, Hoffman's recorded two podiums and three top-fives in the track's last four 100-lap crown jewels. His third-place finish in last year's World was his best in six A-main starts, continue to fuel his Eldora-biggie-winning potential. Sunday's Baltes Classic victory snapped a three-month winless drought and supplied a timely boost entering World week.

7. Hudson O'Neal (71), Martinsville, Ind.

Background: The 16-time winner this year leads the nation with 45 podiums and 76 top-10 finishes, giving him an undeniable résumé. The 2023 World winner has nonetheless gone winless with his SSI Motorsports team since mid-May, a lengthy drought that doesn't mix well with recent World results of 11th and 25th since his 2023 triumph.

Background: Rolling into World week hungry to redeem a likely Dream podium lost to a wheel issue, Erb has three victories in his last six starts, including a win at half-mile Southern Iowa Speedway and a sweep of Portsmouth's $25,000 weekend. He followed that surge with a fifth-place finish in Sunday's Baltes Classic. After charging from 16th to fourth in last year's World, Erb possesses the dangerous combination of proven Eldora speed and timely momentum.

Background: Madden's elusive Eldora crown jewel remains one of Dirt Late Model racing's great unfinished stories after runner-up finishes in three Dreams, the Eldora Million and Dirt Track World Championship. After calling June's Dream DNQ "a total disaster," Madden returns encouraged by consecutive fourth-place finishes at half-mile Port Royal. A breakthrough would certainly carry shades of Dale Earnhardt's cathartic 1998 Daytona 500 victory.

Background: The reigning Lucas Oil Late Model Dirt Series champ enters World week refreshed after Sunday's Hillbilly 100 victory snapped a 21-race winless drought. The breakthrough added another 100-lap triumph to a seven-win season that also includes the Firecracker 100. His World résumé remains surprisingly modest, however, with a single top-five and three top-10s in 10 A-main starts.

Background: The 2021 World winner has eight victories across six tours, but none against a full field since April 15 at Volunteer Speedway; his latest came in an August North-South 100 prelim. He slipped from ninth to 13th in June's Dream after running third in last year's World before pitting on lap 37 and retiring on lap 70. He's still among contenders, qualifying for six straight World A-mains.

Background: Blair has a strong grasp of the Dream, improving from 10th to seventh to second in three appearances while gaining 22 positions overall. His fifth-place finish in the 2024 Dirt Track World Championship and recent 100-lap victory at Lernerville further validate his long-distance strength. Now he must solve the World, where he has qualified only once in three attempts and finished 27th last year.

Background: The complexion of Marlar's season shifted dramatically after he switched to a Rocket XR2 following his Dream DNQ, producing six wins, 10 podiums and 11 top-10s in 22 starts since. He has qualified for eight of the last 10 Worlds, highlighted by a runner-up finish in 2021, but placed 11th in last year's consolation. Few drivers are riding higher into World week.

Background: Like Marlar, the North-South 100 winner has upped his game since debuting a new Rocket XR2, collecting four wins and six podiums across his last 11 starts. Three consecutive podiums at Portsmouth and Eldora over the weekend eased concerns raised by non-factor finishes of 10th and 17th at half-mile Port Royal two weeks ago. The 2025 Dream prelim winner has qualified for four consecutive Worlds, twice finishing a career-best 14th.

Background: The two-time Eldora major winner is the quintessential glass-half-full-or-half-empty contender. Both victories this season came in World of Outlaws events on half-miles at Selinsgrove and Bedford, and he finished second at half-mile Adams County two weeks ago. But he missed June's Dream by one position, while last year's 19th-place World finish ended a streak of six consecutive top-10s.

16. Ryan Gustin (19R), Marshalltown, Iowa

Background: Gustin might be ranked a bit low considering his last three World finishes of eighth, ninth and fifth, but it's difficult to justify placing him ahead of anyone above him.

17. Chris Ferguson (22), Mount Holly, N.C.

articles.title: Bengals’ Zac Taylor announces injury update for Ja’Marr Chase, Tee Higgins
articles.summary: Cincinnati Bengals QB Joe Burrow gets major help for the NFL Week 1 opener as Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins continue their recovery from injury.
articles.body:
The Cincinnati Bengals are preparing for their NFL season opener with Joe Burrow leading an offense that still revolves around Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins . Cincinnati will host the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday at Paycor Stadium, beginning a season that comes with high expectations after another busy offseason. Burrow enters the season with his two primary receivers healthy enough to practice after both dealt with injuries late in the preseason. Chase hyperextended his knee during a joint practice, while Higgins has been dealing with a heel contusion. Both missed practice last week before returning Monday. Burrow and the Bengals need both receivers available as Chase and Higgins are two established targets who can win against man coverage.

Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins on pace to play Sunday

Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Tee Higgins (5). Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images.

Head Coach Zac Taylor said Chase and Higgins are on pace to play against Tampa Bay . The Bengals coach had previously said both receivers would be limited during the week but expected them to be ready for the opener. Chase returned Monday after dealing with the knee issue, while Higgins also got back on the field. Their progress through the rest of the week will determine whether they enter Sunday without a game-status designation or carry one into the opener.

Joe Burrow gets his top weapons back for Week 1

The Bengals spent the offseason improving the roster around Burrow. Cincinnati added Dexter Lawrence and Jonathan Allen to the defensive line while also continuing to build around its established offensive core. Burrow has also made clear that he remains committed to Cincinnati and believes the offseason changes have put the team in a better position entering 2026. Having Chase and Higgins available gives Burrow the best version of his passing attack to start the season. Cincinnati's offense has little room for error after a 6-11 season in 2025, and the team has made significant changes around its quarterback. For a Bengals team trying to return to the playoffs, that is exactly how the offense needs to begin.

articles.title: Blue Jays could compete with Dodgers for Cy Young-winning ace in free agency
articles.summary: The Blue Jays could get into another bidding war with the Dodgers this offseason.
articles.body:
The Toronto Blue Jays and Los Angeles Dodgers have been linked to each other for the past few seasons, especially since they went head-to-head in their pursuit of Shohei Ohtani . He went to the Dodgers, and the Blue Jays missed out.

But they made the World Series and had the Dodgers down to their last gasp; a homer to send the game to extras resulted in a heartbreaking Game 7 loss. Then, over the offseason, the two competed for Kyle Tucker before he chose the Dodgers.

Looking ahead to the 2026-2027 free agency window, the Blue Jays and Dodgers could compete again. CBS Sports' Mike Axisa named the Blue Jays and Dodgers as landing spots for Cy Young free agent ace Tarik Skubal for what could be another bidding war.

Blue Jays and Dodgers could get into a bidding war for Tarik Skubal

"Skubal is the clear-cut, inarguable No. 1 free agent," Axisa writes. "Super early possible landing spots: Blue Jays, Dodgers."

The Blue Jays are a real possible destination for Skubal in free agency. Their ownership group isn't afraid to spend money, and someone like Skubal would be just the kind of player worth splurging on.

He's going to cost a fortune, most likely north of $300 million overall, and potentially even beyond $400 million. But while expensive, the Blue Jays are a logical landing spot.

Pairing him with Dylan Cease could give the Blue Jays the elite 1-2 punch that many elite teams look for in their starting rotation.

Skubal has a 2.84 ERA in a down season by his standards. Cease is a strong Cy Young candidate in the AL this season. Having both pitchers, alongside Trey Yesavage and Jose Soriano, would make for an elite rotation.

Adding Skubal in free agency will be tricky, as they're going to have to outbid the Dodgers. It won't be easy, but if there's any team that could do it, it would be the Blue Jays.

They've gone head-to-head in the free agent market for a lot of the top players over the years, and maybe this time, to land Skubal, they'll come away as the winners.

articles.title: Miami's Toney, Pitt's Heintschel, Duke's Sheppard give ACC national leaders in FBS headlining stats
articles.summary: Malachi Toney couldn't be stopped, running free through Stanford's defense and striking Heisman Trophy poses after catching touchdown passes for seventh-rank...
articles.body:
Malachi Toney couldn't be stopped, running free through Stanford's defense and striking Heisman Trophy poses after catching touchdown passes for seventh-ranked Miami .

A day later, Pittsburgh's Mason Heintschel set an Atlantic Coast Conference single-game record for TD throws. And Nate Sheppard had a tough-running edge that carried Duke all day.

The ACC hasn't had a good start in marquee matchups against other power-conference teams. But the league enters Week 2 with at least one highlight: that sophomore trio posted the top receiving, passing and rushing totals in the Bowl Subdivision ranks, offering hope that there's the kind of skill-position talent that could help the ACC recover from its early hole.

"Because of the movement of the players and the transactional nature of the sport, we've spread the talent thinner so everybody's more competitively balanced," ESPN and ACC Network analyst Tom Luginbill said. "Which means you're going to be in more one-possession games than you've probably ever been in before. ... If you (win) that and you have top performances, now you start shifting the narrative.

"And it draws eyeballs. People are going to say, 'Wait, who's this guy? I haven't seen him.'"

That's not necessary for Toney, who thrived as Miami reached last year's College Football Playoff championship game and was a preseason Associated Press first-team All-American . Heintschel and Sheppard lack that same spotlight yet opened with starring performances, too.

Sophomore trio put up big stats amid ACC's bumpy start

Each was more productive than counterparts anywhere in the country:

Toney had a school-record 234 yards receiving against the Cardinal and is the only FBS player to crack the 200-yard mark through two weekends. His 12 catches were tied for most in a game.

Heintschel threw for a national-best 453 yards in a win against Miami (Ohio) , joining ACC quarterbacks Kevin Jennings of SMU (430 against Florida State) and Darian Mensah of Miami (401 while peppering Toney with targets) as FBS' only passers yet to surpass the 400-yard mark. Heintschel's seven TD throws broke the ACC record of six, which had been reached 11 times.

Sheppard ran for a national-best 227 yards with two TDs in a win against Tulane . Sheppard's 35 carries are the most of any FBS player this year and one of only two FBS performances of at least 30 carries.

Those offered individual highlights as the ACC went 1-5 against the Big 12, Big Ten and Southeastern Conference. North Carolina's win against TCU in Ireland stands as the lone victory in matchups that included No. 8 LSU running Clemson out of Baton Rouge in a game between marquee brands.

Toney finds immediate connection with Mensah

The 5-foot-11, 193-pound Toney delivered 1,211 yards and 10 touchdowns as a freshman, then opened with a dominant performance.

On Miami's first offensive snap at Stanford, he took a short pass to the left and got loose for a 48-yard gain before snagging a 23-yard TD throw. He also had a 2-yard TD grab and went deep for a 47-yard TD in the third quarter.

Toney said afterward that he had gotten faster since last year, while Miami coach Mario Cristobal called Toney an "elite route-runner." That combination helped Mensah post his own fast start with five TD throws after a high-profile transfer from Duke .

"Honestly just makes my job extremely easy as a quarterback," Mensah told reporters Tuesday. "He's almost like another quarterback on the field, just the way that he understands defense."

Heintschel's Year 1 experience shows to start Year 2

Pittsburgh coach Pat Narduzzi went to Heintschel as his starter about a month into last season . Heintschel said in July he felt he had more freedom to work in coordinator Kade Bell's offense with that experience.

He certainly looked in control against the RedHawks while completing 31 of 41 passes (75.6%).

"Coach Bell and I talk about that a lot," Heintschel said. "Take what the defense is giving us. (It's about) just kind of being boring sometimes."

He's the first FBS quarterback since LSU's Joe Burrow in 2019 to throw for at least 450 yards and seven TDs without an interception. Each TD throw went to a different receiver.

"It's very impactful," sophomore running back Ja'Kyrian Turner said. "The defense doesn't know what to do. The threat of Mason is him spreading out the offense. He's got a lot of playmakers he can get the ball to, and plenty of ways to get the offense going."

Sheppard carries a heavy workload in Week 1

With Mensah's move south, it was clear that the reigning ACC champion Blue Devils would lean on Sheppard after he ran for 1,132 yards and 11 TDs last year. Duke did exactly that Saturday, with Sheppard carrying the ball 10 times during a 17-play season-opening drive.

Add three catches, and Sheppard had 38 touches on Duke's 77 offensive plays (49.4%). So managing workload and health will be important going forward.

"He took the bulk of the carries last year, especially the second half of the season," offensive coordinator Jonathan Brewer said Monday. "I don't think this is new to him. Maybe direct runs instead of moreso lighter boxes, RPO type of runs — that kind of stuff is probably a little bit different. He probably had more touches on checkdowns last year than he did in that first game for us.

AP Sports Writer Will Graves in Pittsburgh contributed to this report.

articles.title: With Keider Montero on baby watch, Tigers tentatively juggle rotation
articles.summary: AJ Hinch keeping eye on the career-high level workloads of young right-handers Keider Montero and Troy Melton.
articles.body:
DETROIT — You'd never know it. He continues to go about his business with a carefree smile on his face. But Keider Montero has a lot of his plate these days. His fiancé is pregnant and expected to deliver soon.

There was some trepidation, even, over whether he'd be able to make his start in the series finale against the Twins on Wednesday, Sept. 9. Which, even as rain delayed the start of the game, he was prepared to do.

His fiancé is in Venezuela with no visa. So, Montero's only contact with her has been through FaceTime. The separation has also stalled their wedding plans.

The expectation is Montero will take paternity leave soon. The Tigers have already tentatively juggled their rotation in anticipation of his absence. Manager AJ Hinch said that Framber Valdez will start the series opener against the Rockies on Friday and Jackson Jobe will start Sunday.

"Keider is on baby watch and that's great," Hinch said. "We don't really know exactly what day that's going to happen. We're trying to anticipate and prepare our guys to potentially cover the back side when Keider would pitch again. But I don't know quite yet how that's going to play out."

The off day Thursday gives him some room to maneuver the rotation. Montero's next start after Wednesday would be Monday in Toronto . By pushing the rotation back an extra day, Troy Melton , Drew Anderson and Valdez could start in the three games in Toronto Sept. 14-16.

As for Saturday's start, if Montero goes on the paternity list, the Tigers could recall lefty Andrew Sears from Toledo, even though he was optioned on Sept. 5.

None of that has been decided. What has been decided, though, is that the workloads of both Montero and Melton will be under scrutiny in these next two-plus weeks.

Montero went into his start Wednesday having thrown a career-high 143 innings and more than 2,000 pitches. Melton, who missed spring training and the first two months of the season with an elbow injury, is at 108 innings. He threw 54 big-league innings last season, including 8.1 in the postseason, plus 75 innings in the minors.

Hinch and pitching coach Chris Fetter are trying to balance health and safety with conditioning pitchers to run the full race. Which, as Hinch pointed out, isn't supposed to end in September.

"We're going to be careful," Hinch said. "But it's important for guys to go start to finish. We talk about workload right now and the nervousness that comes when pitchers get to uncharted territory. But we're only in early September. We're not even to the hard sprint to October which is when we want to play. You have to be really careful not to condition young players that now is the time to be guarded."

Hinch said with the off day Thursday, he can be a little more wary Montero, especially if he's going on paternity leave. And by leaving the Saturday start date open against Colorado , Melton will get two extra days, or more if Hinch wants to push him to the end of the Blue Jays series.

"I want to be very clear with them, the goal isn't just to finish at the end of September," he said. "We have to train for an extra month. October baseball is as intense as it gets."

The message is the same for position players.

"If Dillon (Dingler) is tired or Kevin (McGonigle) is beat up, yes, it happens in September," Hinch said. "But we want these guys preparing to play another 40 days, not another 15. That mentality has to be pushed on all of us."

articles.title: Why Jeff Hafley should keep it simple with these young Dolphins
articles.summary: What the NFL's youngest roster needs from Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley
articles.body:
MIAMI GARDENS ― During the preseason, including joint practices, Miami Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley was open about keeping schemes simple.

The key, Hafley explained, was getting a complete evaluation of the players.

It was not about tricking opponents with complex strategies.

It's my opinion that Hafley should take a similar approach in the regular season, starting with the season-opener at Las Vegas on Sunday, Sept. 13.

Keep it simple. Less complex. Limit risk.

Recently I asked Hafley about if he'll use his "gut" to potentially override some in-game recommendations from the analytics teams, such as punting or going for it on fourth down.

"I think you have a plan, and I think a lot of the times you try to stick with your plan, but there's always got to be the feel of the game and where it's going and the momentum of the game and how I think everything is going and what the team needs from me right now," Hafley said.

Much of the strategy will be determined the week before the game. Stick with the plan.

Miami is currently an underdog in 16 of 17 regular-season games. But the Dolphins have a shot on Sunday.

Photos of Miami Dolphins 53-man roster - until they add/drop players

Miami Dolphins roster is youngest in NFL

They're only 3.5-point underdogs and facing a beatable quarterback, Kirk Cousins .

If rookie Fernando Mendoza was making his first career start, it might make more sense to throw a few "kitchen sinks" at the youngster.

But Cousins has seen everything. There is no need to throw a bunch of blitzes at him that may confuse Miami's 14-member rookie class more than Cousins.

Keep it simple. Give the team a chance. Help limit busts from a very inexperienced secondary.

Blowouts can be demoralizing for a young group. Limiting blowouts could prove beneficial in the long-run.

Go for it on 4th-and-1 from Miami's 39-yard line on the first possession of the season?

We say punt. And that hurts to write. But punt.

Limit short fields for the defense. Limit tons of snaps for the defense. This team lacks depth.

Dolphins could play it conservative early on

Hafley noted he was among the leaders in going for it on fourth down at Boston College one season.

At times, BC was undermanned in a manner similar to what the Dolphins figure to face this year.

The goal this season is to, yes, try to win some games. But even more important is to evaluation of players, particularly young players.

Former Dolphins coach Dave Wannstedt, a mentor of Hafley's, used to say in so many words that the punt is not a bad play (certainly compared to a turnover on downs, interception or lost fumble).

Times have changed. Far more teams now are going for it on 4th-and-1.

But tapping into some of Wannstedt's mindset this season would not be the worst thing.

Could Miami roll out an exotic blitz here or later there this season?

Sure. But starting out "base" and "vanilla" seems the best way to go early in the season.

"I'm going to call what I believe our guys can execute at a high level," Hafley said, a few days before the opener.

Miami needs to evaluate their players in 1-on-1 situations this season. It's far less essential to scheme up free runners or 2-on-1's. Evaluation must be key to every decision.

Miami Dolphins ' Jeff Hafley could keep it vanilla early on

Miami has the youngest roster in the league. Keep it simple.

I once asked a college coach about how fast a young player was.

"That's great but if you're running the wrong way, you just get there faster," he said.

Miami figures to have some rookies running fast, but the wrong way on Sunday.

Keep it simple. Limit mistakes. Just play fast and free.

The New York Yankees received encouraging injury updates on Ryan Weathers and Fernando Cruz . Weathers has progressed to throwing from 75 feet while recovering from a left forearm flexor strain, while Cruz could soon resume throwing as he takes a non-surgical approach to a partially torn right UCL.

The updates provide New York with clearer recovery timelines as the club enters the final three weeks of the regular season at 82-62 and atop the AL wild-card standings. MLB.com's latest Yankees injury report outlined the next steps for both pitchers as they work toward potential returns.

"LHP Ryan Weathers Injury: Left forearm flexor strain IL date: Aug. 23 (15-day-IL) Expected return: Late September Status: Threw from 75 feet (40 throws) on Sept. 8, with plans to repeat process the next two days. Could begin throwing off a mound when he resumes after a day off on Sept. 11."

Met with Dr. Keith Meister, who advised a conservative approach for now. May resume throwing weekend of Sept. 11."

Weathers is further along in his recovery after throwing 40 times from 75 feet on Tuesday. He planned to repeat that work on Wednesday and Thursday before a scheduled day off, then he could progress to mound work.

The 26-year-old landed on the injured list after leaving his August 22 start against the Toronto Blue Jays . Imaging showed no structural damage. Before the injury, Weathers posted a 3.60 ERA with 143 strikeouts across 137 1/3 innings.

Cruz faces a less certain timetable with a partial tear in his right UCL. Dr. Keith Meister recommended a conservative approach, and he could resume throwing this weekend.

articles.title: Rutgers men's basketball coach Steve Pikiell reveals cancer diagnosis
articles.summary: Rutgers coach Steve Pikiell said he plans to be still be involved with the team as he udnergoes chemotherapy.
articles.body:
Pikiell announced on Wednesday, Sept. 9 he was not feeling 100% a few months ago and visited the team doctors, and after undergoing testing, he learned he has cancer. He did not disclose what type of cancer it was.

"I am incredibly grateful to my team of doctors at RWJBarnabas Health and Memorial Sloan Kettering for guiding and supporting us through this difficult time," he said in a statement . "After a successful surgery, my doctors and I have a kick-ass game plan to finish treatment."

Pikiell still plans to be involved with the team "to the best of my ability" as he undergoes chemotherapy in the coming months, but associate head coach Brandin Knight will be at the helm when Pikiell is unable to.

Rutgers athletic director Keli Zinn said there is no set timeline for when Pikiell will be able to fully return to the team.

"We are grateful to Coach Knight for his willingness to step up during this challenging time and to our entire staff for their great care and compassion for Coach and our student-athletes," Zinn said.

Pikiell arrived at Rutgers in 2016 and led the Scarlet Knights to the NCAA Tournament in 2021, their first apperance in 30 years, and winning its first tournament game in 38 years. Rutgers again made the tournament the following season.

In 10 seasons in Piscataway, Pikiell is 161–160.

Knight has been at Rutgers since Pikiell's arrival in 2016, elevating his way from assistant to associate coach.

Rutgers opens the 2026-27 season against New Haven on Nov. 6.

articles.summary: El gesto de Álvaro Montero en Boca Juniors tras una dolorosa pérdida familiar
articles.body: Álvaro Montero disputó los 90 minutos en la victoria 1-0 de Boca Juniors frente a São Paulo por la Copa Sudamericana, a pesar de enterarse del fallecimiento de su abuela antes del encuentro. Transcurrido el partido, emprendió viaje a Colombia para acompañar a su familia. Álvaro Montero firmó una actuación sobresaliente bajo los tres palos del Xeneize en el duelo de ida de los cuartos de final de la CONMEBOL Sudamericana ante São Paulo. El portero colombiano fue determinante con tres atajadas clave, entre ellas un manotazo milagroso ante un cabezazo de Luciano en la primera mitad y un bloqueo firme en el área chica para sostener el cero en el arco. Sin embargo, detrás del triunfo 1-0 conseguido gracias al gol de Miguel Merentiel, se escondía una dura noticia familiar. En la conferencia de prensa posterior al compromiso, el director técnico de Boca Juniors reveló el difícil momento personal que atravesaba el guardameta samario: "Hoy, antes del partido, falleció la abuela y ahora está viajando a Colombia. Es un golpe duro para él, pero estuvo presente e hizo una gran actuación. Me pone contento mantener el arco en cero ante un rival importante", declaró el entrenador. El estratega xeneize también aprovechó para respaldar el proceso de adaptación de Montero en el club argentino, destacando su tranquilidad frente a las críticas y su progresiva consolidación como titular.

articles.title: Javi Garrido y Lucas Bergamini caen en el Paris Major y anuncian su separación
articles.standfirst: El cordobés y el brasileño ponen fin a su proyecto conjunto tras ceder en los dieciseisavos de final en Roland Garros
articles.summary: El cordobés y el brasileño ponen fin a su proyecto conjunto tras ceder en los dieciseisavos de final en Roland Garros
articles.body: La jornada de dieciseisavos de final del Paris Major no solo dejó una de las sorpresas en el cuadro masculino, sino que conllevó la separación de los propios damnificados. Javi Garrido y Lucas Bergamini no pudieron superar su debut en el torneo francés y, tras la derrota, confirmaron que no continuarán compitiendo juntos. El cordobés y el brasileño se estrenaban en la cita parisina ante Javi Martínez y Luis Hernández Quesada. Pese a que Garrido y Bergamini partían como novenos cabezas de serie del torneo, Martínez y Hernández llevaron la iniciativa desde los primeros compases del choque, abrochando el primer set con un claro 6-1. La segunda manga ofreció una mayor paridad, pero terminó resolviéndose en el tie-break a favor de la pareja española (7-6), consumando la eliminación de los favoritos. Tras el encuentro, Garrido hizo oficial la ruptura a través de sus perfiles en redes sociales. El dueto hispano-brasileño atravesaba una racha compleja de resultados, sumando en París su sexto torneo consecutivo en Premier Padel sin alcanzar los cuartos de final y enlazando tres eliminaciones en su primer compromiso. “Berguita, te agradezco de corazón todo el esfuerzo que has hecho durante todo este año. Es una pena que no hayamos podido disfrutar y competir como lo hemos hecho a diario. Te deseo lo mejor del mundo siempre”, expuso el jugador andaluz en su cuenta de Instagram. La disolución de esta pareja provocará nuevos cambios en la zona media de la clasificación FIP. En función de si el movimiento se concreta mediante un intercambio directo de compañeros o través de fichajes individuales, la reestructuración afectará a varios proyectos del circuito. En las posiciones de ranking en las que se ubican tanto Garrido como Bergamini coinciden duplas que han atravesado dinámicas diversas. Es el caso de Momo González y Lucas Campagnolo, proyecto que comenzó con buenos resultados antes de sufrir un parón de efectividad; o de Javi Leal y Fran Guerrero, que mantienen una posición sólida aunque han mostrado altibajos en sus últimas actuaciones. Por su parte, duplas como la formada por Maxi Arce y Juan Tello podrían valorar un ajuste para mejorar su posición como cabezas de serie en los próximos cuadros. Asimismo, la presencia en el mercado de perfiles como Edu Alonso o Jairo Bautista abre diferentes alternativas para la recomposición de parejas en este tramo de la temporada, a la espera de que los propios jugadores confirmen sus inscripciones para los siguientes torneos del calendario oficial.

articles.title: Post-Travis Hunter, Colorado And Coach Prime Have A 380-Pound 2-Way Player
articles.summary: Colorado interior lineman Chauncey Gooden is a 380-pound lineman who played both offense and defense in a season-opening win against Georgia Tech.
articles.body: The newest two-way player for the Colorado Buffaloes is listed at 380 pounds and enjoys nothing more than throwing that weight around in the trenches. Sophomore Chauncey Gooden has developed into the interior lineman version of former Colorado receiver and cornerback Travis Hunter. Gooden's primary responsibilities are at left guard and keeping quarterback Julian Lewis well-protected. But in goal-line and short-yardage situations, the second-year player from Nashville, Tennessee, uses his 6-foot-3 frame to help clog up the middle. In a season-opening 14-13 comeback win at Georgia Tech, Gooden played 65 offensive snaps and another seven on defense. He was the lone interior lineman in the Division I ranks last week to play both ways, according to research provided from the school. There was no real lobbying for the assignment, either. It was just showing coach Deion Sanders that he could excel at an elite level on the offensive line. Once he did that, more responsibility was heaped onto his plate. "Coach Prime just gave me the opportunity, like, ‘Chauncey, what can you do on that D-line?’" said Gooden, who was named the Outland Trophy national player of the week on Wednesday for his work on the line of scrimmage. "I was like, ‘Coach, I can go over here and show you now.’ So I went over there. I was just causing havoc and being myself and things like that. Next thing you know, he just trusted me to throw me in there." The rules for playing both ways Memo to any other Buffaloes who want to play both ways: No need to mention it to Sanders. "You’d be a fool to just tell me ‘I want to play both ways’. I should know that coming in," said Sanders, whose team hosts Weber State (1-1) on Saturday afternoon with a chance to improve to 2-0. "When I recruited you, I should have known that’s part of it. You can’t just approach me and say, ‘I want play both ways.’ Then I’m going to say, ‘I want to see you play one way really good. Let’s do that first.’ That’s mainly the criteria." Sanders pointed out that even Hunter had to prove himself. He was primarily a receiver during his first spring in Boulder before getting the chance to shine on defense. "Once he dominated one side, it was easy to say, ‘OK, now let’s venture off to the other one,’" Sanders explained. "He earned his right to get on that other side and do his thing. Chauncey’s earned it." Other players to play both ways at Colorado under Sanders include cornerback and receiver Isaiah Hardge and lineman Tyler Brown. Gooden considers it an honor to even draw the smallest comparison to Hunter, the 2024 Heisman Trophy winner now in his second season with the Jacksonville Jaguars. Hunter averaged roughly 120 snaps per game that season, which makes Gooden appreciate the feat even more. "Best player to do that," Gooden said. "The fact that I can do what he did even in the trenches, it’s just remarkable." The run game Gooden played a part in helping a defensive front limit Georgia Tech to 51 yards rushing. On the offensive side, the Buffaloes ran it 49 times — the most in the Sanders era at Colorado — for 183 yards. The "Go-Go" offense, installed by new coordinator Brennan Marion, is certainly a hit with the offensive linemen. "We can play free and physical," Gooden said. Gooden improved his stamina in preparation for playing both ways. He recalled an exchange with Sanders during camp, when the coach told his guard that if he went all-out at a certain portion of practice, extra conditioning would be canceled. "So I go out there, and I pancake two people straight," Gooden said of knocking his defensive teammates to the turf. "He was trying to get through my head." The ploy worked — even if it turned out to be a ruse. We had a long conversation about that after practice," cracked Gooden, who saw action in the final four games last season as the team finished 3-9. "I trust Coach Prime and what he's got to do for me." Gooden arrived at Colorado after playing at Lipscomb Academy in Nashville, where he worked at times with NFL Hall of Fame offensive lineman Kevin Mawae and Super Bowl-winning quarterback Trent Dilfer. It fostered discipline, which serves him well in Boulder. "Coach Prime told me to just be me out there on that field. Be that dawg," Gooden said. "He just brings me the confidence to be able to go out there and get the job done." Reporting by The Associated Press.

articles.summary: Momentos de angustia: así fue el fallido aterrizaje del Independiente Medellín en el aeropuerto de Pasto
articles.body: Lo que debía ser un desplazamiento rutinario para afrontar su compromiso deportivo por la Copa BetPlay terminó convirtiéndose en un momento de tensión y angustia para la delegación del Independiente Medellín. Un video difundido en redes sociales y medios de comunicación evidenció el dramático momento que vivieron los integrantes del equipo antioqueño tras sufrir tres intentos fallidos de aterrizaje en la ciudad de Pasto debido a las adversas condiciones climáticas. En la grabación captada por uno de los viajeros se percibe el clima de preocupación a bordo de la aeronave en el momento en que los pilotos intentaban el descenso en el Aeropuerto Antonio Nariño, caracterizado históricamente por la complejidad de sus corrientes de aire y topografía. El equipo pasará la noche en la capital del Valle y este miércoles sobre las 10:00 a.m. tomará vuelo nuevamente a la ciudad de Pasto”. El imprevisto meteorológico alteró por completo la planificación deportiva del Poderoso de la Montaña. La plantilla debió pernoctar en la capital vallecaucana antes de reprogramar el trayecto matutino hacia la capital de Nariño para disputar su encuentro programado. articles.title: Mina Kimes thinks perception of Dianna Russini-Mike Vrabel scandal is unfair to women
articles.summary: Mina Kimes says the Dianna Russini and Mike Vrabel scandal gives bad-faith actors license to target women working in sports media nationwide.
articles.body: ESPN analyst Mina Kimes says the scandal involving former NFL reporter Dianna Russini and New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel has given bad-faith actors an excuse to target women. For background, an ESPN report earlier this week cited anonymous female reporters who claimed the scandal has caused them to navigate their jobs differently. "One reporter said an assistant coach told her he would not want to be seen meeting her for a coffee, specifically citing the optics of the Vrabel-Russini situation," ESPN reported. Kimes discussed the report on a podcast with Charlotte Wilder this week, accusing fans of creating a negative narrative around women in sports. "I think it reflects sort of a broader thing that happens in any industry, which is when someone who’s not in the majority makes any sort of error, it becomes a referendum for their entire class," Kimes said. She added that critics are not applying the same standards to other insiders. "Giving license to male sports fans generally to speak about them a certain way, or to honestly talk about this story in a way that they don’t with other stories involving lapses in journalism. It’s been interesting to watch on the Russini side of it, this massive conversation on the internet about, ‘This is a crime against journalism, and no one’s talking about it’ … it’s kind of hard to take those critiques in good faith when they’re clearly not coming from a place of, these aren’t people who actually care about journalism." Kimes added. Wilder took a more pointed stance, accusing fans of misogyny. "It seems to me that to blame one woman for making a mistake and saying that she has screwed it up for everybody else, nobody does that for men," Wilder said. "I understand that it is different; she was in a very high-profile position, but it doesn’t sit right, I don’t think." "It gives license to people, perhaps, who are looking for an excuse to not treat women the same way, and then run with it," she added. Got all that? MATTHEW BERRY DISCUSSES WHETHER HE'D HIRE DIANNA RUSSINI FOR HIS BUDDING FANTASY FOOTBALL EMPIRE Kimes and Wilder did not add much substance to the conversation, but the ESPN report is notable. For months, various women in sports media have expressed concerns to OutKick that Russini’s blunder could reflect negatively on them. It is also understandable that male officials around the league would now be more cognizant of spending time alone with female reporters, given the potential narratives. Granted, these dynamics were in place long before photos surfaced of Russini hugging and holding hands with a current football coach. The perception of relationships between men and women will always be viewed differently by some observers. The same would be true if a male reporter were alone with a female coach in the WNBA. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! We would, however, push back on Wilder’s claim that Russini "screwed it up" for all women. While coaches and officials might be more careful around female reporters, the general view of women in the industry has not changed. No honest media executive or source thinks differently of Stacey Dales, Charissa Thompson, Laura Rutledge, Erin Andrews, Sage Steele or other top women in sports media because of Russini’s photos. Kimes and Wilder seem to be, predictably, putting too much stock in what anonymous social media trolls post. For example, ESPN reporter Taylor McGregor gained national attention this week for her stellar on-air reporting during the Florida State-SMU power outage. No serious person questioned her credentials because Russini allegedly spent time on a boat with Vrabel while she was seven months pregnant. Kimes and, especially, Wilder appear to want to make this dynamic larger than it is. The Russini story is not going to be a roadblock in their careers. articles.summary: En la tercera jornada del Europeo de Turquía, España sumó nueve medallas más
articles.body: Teresa Perales es insaciable. La nadadora maña se colgó este miércoles su tercera medalla europea consecutiva en Kocaeli (Turquía) y la número 98 de su cuenta particular internacional: Juegos (28), Mundiales (23) y Europeos (47). También subió al podio Emma Feliu en los 100 libre S13. Su 1:00.92 le valió el bronce. La italiana Carlotta Gilli se impuso en la prueba (1:00.21) y la irlandesa Roisin Ni Riain fue plata (1:00.52). Marian Polo terminó cuarta (1:01.80) y Ariadna Edo, octava (1:03.97). Por su parte, María Delgado e Íñigo Llopis lograron sendas cuartas posiciones en 50 libre S12 y 100 mariposa S8, con tiempos de 29.27 y 1:05.76, respectivamente. articles.title: Gavin McKenna to Live with Maple Leafs Teammate John Tavares During Rookie NHL Season
articles.summary: Gavin McKenna will have a veteran housemate for his first season with the Toronto Maple Leafs.
articles.body:
Gavin McKenna will have a veteran housemate for his first season with the Toronto Maple Leafs.

John Tavares told reporters Tuesday the top pick of the 2026 NHL draft will be living in his house this season, per The Athletic's Mark Lazerus .

According to Lazerus, the arrangement took place after Tavares and his wife, Aryne, told Leafs general manager John Chayka they were interested in hosting McKenna.

Trades That Could Happen Before Training Camp

"You want him to go out and enjoy all the great things about being a Maple Leaf, and living his dream, playing in the NHL... and when it does feel heavy at times, or when it is a lot, going through it for the first time, he has that ability to just be in a family environment," Tavares said, per Lazerus.

This isn't the first time Tavares has hosted a Leafs rookie. Players including Fraser Minten and Matthew Knies have lived with the Tavares family since the forward signed with the Leafs in 2018.

Tavares most recently hosted Easton Cowan last season, per The Hockey News' Michael Traikos .

The Athletic's Joshua Kloke reported last October Cowan had credited Tavares with teaching him self-care routines that helped him make the Leafs roster.

McKenna was selected at the top of the 2026 draft after a record-breaking three WHL seasons followed by a point-per-game freshman campaign for Penn State.

He will now become the latest top draft pick to start out his NHL career by sharing a house with a more experienced teammate.

Macklin Celebrini lived with San Jose Sharks icon Joe Thornton after being selected at the top of the 2024 draft, a year before 2025 top pick Matthew Schaefer moved in with New York Islanders vet Matt Martin.

Tavares, the first pick of the 2009 draft, spent the first two years of his own NHL career living with former Islanders forward Doug Weight.

After five seasons captaining the Isles, Tavares served as captain for five more seasons in Toronto before he passed the C on to Auston Matthews ahead of the 2025-26 campaign.

Tavares will still be taking on a major leadership role in his eighth season with the Leafs. His ability to guide McKenna could be key in helping the rookie winger develop into a linemate for Matthews.

articles.title: Leo Carlsson Says NHL 'Players Are Thanking Me' After Ducks Matched Historic Contract Offer Sheet
articles.summary: Leo Carlsson signed a massive five-year, $92 million offer sheet with the Philadelphia Flyers this summer, which the Anaheim Ducks ultimately matched.
articles.body:
Leo Carlsson signed a massive five-year, $92 million offer sheet with the Philadelphia Flyers this summer, which the Anaheim Ducks ultimately matched.

At the time, the deal represented the highest average annual salary in the league, and players around the NHL were apparently very happy that Carlsson upended the market in such a manner:

Trades That Could Happen Before Training Camp

"Obviously it's a huge deal for the league," he told Sportsnet's Sean Reynolds .

The Ducks, meanwhile, made their own bed on this situation.

Anaheim general manager Pat Verbeek has a reputation for trying to squeeze every last penny out of young players in extension talks, a habit that ultimately contributed to players like Jamie Drysdale, Mason McTavish and Trevor Zegras playing elsewhere.

The Ducks had months to exclusively negotiate an extension with Carlsson, who said publicly he would take a deal in the realm of eight years and $76 million, or about half the AAV of the offer sheet he ultimately signed.

Instead, the Ducks didn't get anything done and the Flyers pounced, signing Carlsson to a deal that included around $85 million in guaranteed signing bonuses. It was an offer aimed to prevent the Ducks from matching, though Anaheim ultimately relented.

But there have been repercussions. Veteran forward Chris Kreider was waived Wednesday and restricted free agent Cutter Gauthier remains without a contract. By waiting until Carlsson signed an offer sheet, the Ducks reduced their chances of keeping the current core together.

"Personally, it's a hard question," Carlsson said when asked about the team-building complications that come with one player having a large cap hit. "Everyone feels different. Obviously it's such a weird business, like I don't want to see Chris leave. Hard business, for sure."

But overall, NHL players seem pleased that Carlsson moved the market in the way he did.

articles.title: A’ja Wilson’s old “pettiness” admission sparks new debate after Linda Cohn links her exit to Caitlin Clark

articles.body: A’ja Wilson’s decision to withdraw from Team USA’s FIBA Women’s Basketball World Cup roster has taken another turn after former ESPN host Linda Cohn questioned whether Caitlin Clark’s growing attention played a role. Wilson’s absence was officially linked to health concerns, with reports pointing to a back issue. Now, an old clip of Wilson talking about how “pettiness” fuels her has resurfaced, adding another layer to the debate.A’ja Wilson’s “Pettiness” Comments resurface after Linda Cohn’s Caitlin Clark remarksCohn raised questions about Wilson’s late withdrawal because the specific health issue was not publicly explained by USA Basketball. She wondered whether Wilson wanted to avoid watching the World Cup become centered around Clark.“Could A’ja simply not want to deal with that? Could there be some insecurity, dare I say…could she be thinking, ‘I’m the four-time MVP, I’m the best player in the world, why does everything have to be about Caitlin Clark?’” Cohn said.The comments drew a strong response from South Carolina coach Dawn Staley, who coached Wilson in college. Staley replied to Cohn on X with three simple words: “Linda, please!”The discussion grew again when an older clip of Wilson from Hot Ones resurfaced. In it, she openly admitted that being petty can push her during competition.“Absolutely. It’s sickening. It’s really bad how much pettiness fuels me, but yes. You can talk about anything, I’m gonna find something within it. I don’t like the way you didn’t use punctuation in your tweet. Like, I’m mad. People be testing me, and I love to let them know that I test back. I like to push buttons, too.”That clip does not show Wilson discussing Clark or her World Cup decision. Still, its timing has made the old comments part of the current conversation.Linda Cohn explains Her A’ja Wilson and Caitlin Clark commentsWilson’s withdrawal came shortly before Team USA began its World Cup campaign in Berlin. Reuters reported that USA Basketball listed health reasons for her absence, while reports also noted Wilson had been dealing with a back issue.Cohn later explained that she was questioning the lack of details, rather than claiming she knew Wilson’s real reason for sitting out. “I went right to the source, USA Basketball. It cited health reasons, no details given. I was curious. … So why didn’t USA Basketball know about it? They detailed Kelsey Plum’s injury but not A’ja’s. I was just asking questions.”The numbers also explain why the two players are often compared. Wilson is averaging 26.0 points, 9.4 rebounds and 3.2 assists for the Las Vegas Aces, while Clark is averaging 22.5 points, 3.9 rebounds and a league-best 8.4 assists for the Indiana Fever.The key point, however, is that there is no evidence that Wilson skipped the World Cup because of Clark.
