articles.title: A Complete Timeline Of The Aftermath Of Michigan’s Controversial Win
articles.summary: Breaking down the continued controversy surrounding the Michigan-West Michigan finish, one day at a time.
articles.body: The controversy surrounding the ending of the Western Michigan and Michigan game hasn’t slowed down heading into Week 2. Despite formal appeals, statements and lingering concerns the backlash shows no signs of stopping anytime soon. How much time was actually left? That still hasn’t been determined with so much discrepancy surrounding the play and the cannon of an arm that Wolverines quarterback Bryce Underwood showcased on Saturday night. As things stand now, the call will stand and there will be no action or league involvement. Here’s a timeline of everything that's happened since the controversial call in Ann Arbor: Saturday Night Bryce Underwood Completes Miraculous Hail Mary Michigan entered the matchup as a nearly four-touchdown favorite. However, Western Michigan hung in there and remained competitive until the final whistle, at one point leading 12-6 and standing on the brink of pulling off the biggest upset in program history. However, that lead was put to the ultimate test as the clock hit zero and Underwood unleashed a final Hail Mary. As the ball bounced off multiple defenders in the back of the end zone, the game seemed over... or was it? While the TV broadcast clock showed zero, replay officials came together and confirmed one second remained when the previous pass hit the turf out of bounds. Given one final chance, Underwood this time launched a game-winning Hail Mary touchdown to JJ Buchanan as time expired. The wild final play was only the start of a controversial sequence that would become the talk of the college football world. Later On Saturday Night Kyle Whittingham's Post-Game Reaction Lance Taylor's Post-Game Reaction The controversial call made waves across the sport. Both Michigan coach Kyle Whittingham and Western Michigan coach Lance Taylor shared their thoughts on the final play, which was impactful enough to prompt official statements from both the MAC and the Big Ten. "But as I looked, I knew it was close," Whittingham said after the game. "When the ball sailed back to the end zone, I glanced up at the clock, and it was just ticking to zero, and somebody had touched it. I didn't know who had touched it, but apparently it was a defender that had already established an out-of-bounds position. I'm assuming they got it right. They looked at it and their technology that they have is very advanced, I guess." Even with Whittingham coming out victorious, he offered an honest opinion and backed the officials. Similarly, Taylor focused on why his defense failed to execute as they should have, refusing to make excuses. "I know when I looked up at the clock, it was past zeros before we touched it," Taylor said. I knew that they would review it. It was the last play of the game, and because we defended it so well, wasn't worried or concerned about our guys going out and defending it the second time. Unfortunately, we did not defend it as well the second time." The MAC and Big Ten both issued statements following the game, and everyone accepted the outcome despite the controversy. Sunday Statement Released NBC Sports Releases Statement On Sunday, NBC Sports addressed the growing controversy on air during the Washington vs. Washington State game. Host John Fanta delivered a statement on behalf of the network regarding a clock dispute from the game. He made sure to remind viewers that the TV graphics don't dictate official game time. "Now, the official time of the game is kept by the Big Ten," Fanta said "Our cameras are not the official arbiter of timekeeping within the game. That is the Big Ten and game officials' responsibility. After the game last night, the Big Ten released a statement and raw video from its replay process that showed how and why the decision was made." Monday: Rules and Extra Seconds Continue to Dominate the Conversation Rules Analyst Mike Pereira Joins 'The Joel Klatt Show' When it comes to the rules of the sport and how officials operate, few people are more qualified than FOX Sports rules analyst Mike Pereira. He joined "The Joel Klatt Show" on Monday to break down the latest controversy. His explanation for why Big Ten officials didn't follow protocol focused on the discrepancy, saying that they needed to rely on the television footage. "The official replay officials have been told that if there is a discrepancy, use the television footage," Pereira said. "Do not use your footage in the command center. Use the footage that 10 million people are watching, not the one that's three." Despite heavy criticism of the call, Pereira defended the officials but criticized the review result, stating that the game crew made the best possible decision in real time with the information they had. "When it's all said and done, that's what should have happened, and there shouldn't have been another play," Pereira said. "They did not look at the television copy of what was being shown to all of us." MAC Decides To Appeal Ruling On Tuesday Western Michigan Loses Appeal After initially accepting the ruling, the MAC reversed course and decided to appeal. On Tuesday, MAC Commissioner Jon Steinbrecher released a statement indicating that proper replay protocol was not followed. Following a careful review, the NCAA denied the MAC's appeal, as the Football Bowl Subdivision Oversight Committee stated that it does not have the power to alter the outcome or final score of a game. With that in mind, Michigan remains the winner of the game, even with all the controversy surrounding the result. Both Michigan and Western Michigan will be heading into Week 2 with an outcome that will always be known as the "what-if" game.

articles.body:

articles.title: Coco Gauff ecapes U.S. Open heartbreak as Mirra Andreeva wilts on Arthur Ashe Stadium
articles.summary: NEW YORK — Coco Gauff’s dream of a third Grand Slam title, and a second at the U.S. Open was crashing into a wall Wednesday afternoon. For one set, Mirra And...
articles.body:
NEW YORK — Coco Gauff's dream of a third Grand Slam title, and a second at the U.S. Open was crashing into a wall Wednesday afternoon.

For one set, Mirra Andreeva, the 19-year-old French Open champion, was as solid as she needed to be against an opponent who had one of those sets any tennis player dreads.

Gauff had no feel for the ball. She could not land a first serve with any sort of consistency. Her forehand and serve, which she has been rebuilding in earnest for the past 12 months, fell apart.

Andreeva has been trying to manage the stress of living up to her success in Paris all summer. In New York, Gauff's struggles were the ultimate gift. Andreeva was up 4-0 after 12 minutes, and halfway home after 27, 6-2 to the good.

But then, Gauff's difficulties crossed over the net. Andreeva tightened and started spraying balls of her own. By the middle of the second set, they were embroiled in a tentative push-pull of nerves, neither player able to step in and seize initiative on a point unless they were first forced to do so.

When they went to a tiebreak, Gauff twice faced match point. She tried the only thing that had been working half-decently on the afternoon. She charged ahead, trying to force Andreeva to make a shot to beat her. Andreeva sent a lob long on the first one; Gauff got another error on the second.

From there, Gauff rose as Andreeva unraveled. When she completed the tiebreak escape to level the match at one set all, Gauff sent a roar through her home Slam stadium and sent Andreeva reeling.

Early in the third set, Gauff chased back after a topspin lob and sent it high and deep to Andreeva, who was waiting for it inside the other baseline.

She barely swung at it. It felt like something breaking. Another error on the next point, and Andreeva hurled her racket to the ground, coming dangerously close to hitting a worker.

Her heart had been done since the tiebreak. Now her tennis soul appeared to be missing, too.

Gauff cruised from there, finishing off a 6-2, 7-6(6), 6-2 win and getting the loudest roar yet out of a stadium which, for so long that afternoon, had held its breath.

She will face Elena Rybakina in the semifinals Thursday, in a duel against the new world No. 1.

"These are the moments you dream of," she told the crowd.

articles.title: Gay should open for England in South Africa - Cook
articles.summary: England batter Emilio Gay has done enough to lock in an opener's spot for their winter tour of South Africa, according to Sir Alastair Cook.
articles.body:
England opener Emilio Gay should retain his spot for their winter tour of South Africa, according to former captain Sir Alastair Cook.

Gay made a Test-best 60 from 114 balls to blunt Pakistan's attack which helped England seize control on day one at Edgbaston.

The 26-year-old left-hander's tally of 261 runs, at an average of 26.1, might not look particularly eye-catching.

But in an English summer where ball has dominated bat - Ben Duckett is England's only centurion in six home Tests so far - the Durham left-hander has shown a willingness to grind it out.

Cook, who made almost 12,000 runs as an opener for England, has been impressed with the character the Durham left-hander has shown to make tough runs at the top of the order.

"I think Emilio Gay's played really nicely. I would say he's confident and intense," Cook told Test Match Special.

"He is definitely a run-getter when he gets in. He seems to have that real stubborn and strong will to make it count if he can.

"He has done enough for me to take him to South Africa to continue the progress of a player where the pitches will be slightly easier to bat on and he should open the batting."

According to CricViz, Gay has left or defended 61% of the pace deliveries he's faced since his debut against New Zealand in June.

Dom Sibley in 2020 (68% left or defended) was the last English opener to register a higher percentage in a home summer.

During his innings on Wednesday, Gay left or defended 65 deliveries and Cook "likes how late he defends the ball" with a patient approach to more attacking strokeplay.

Gay scored the first 12 runs of his half-century off 43 balls before his next 38 came off 52 balls.

He hit nine fours and has scored 68% of his Test runs in boundaries - the joint-highest of any England batter with at least 250 runs in the red-ball format.

"If you take Gay's innings, and what I've seen of him, he's not hunting that drive too often. He waits for it to come into there," added Cook.

"He scores off the back foot through the off side as well. He scored through the leg side and timed them through mid-wicket so he does have an all-round game. He's not limited to the off side."

Given Pakistan's flimsy batting - bowled out for 133 in their first innings here - it could end up being Gay's final Test innings of the summer.

With Jacob Bethell set to return for the tour of South Africa following injury, the selection of a top-order batter for the winter is likely to be a scrap between Jordan Cox, Dan Lawrence and Gay for two places.

Only Harry Brook (six occasions) has passed 30 more times than Gay (five) during a challenging summer for batters.

Although Gay has struggled to play back of a length bowling with seven dismissals in the 7-9 metre length range which has highlighted a potential weakness.

Former England captain Michael Vaughan said Gay "played nicely" but might reflect on an missed opportunity to reach three figures for the first time after he dragged on a delivery from Razaullah Khan.

"Emilio Gay found his balance early. He had it hard at the start and then he found his flow," Vaughan said.

"He'll be really disappointed to get out for 60. He'll be desperate to get his first Test match century and I thought it was on today.

"That extra little bit of pace from Razaullah and a little lack of concentration at the end of the day has cost him."

England seamer Josh Tongue said Gay's rigorous preparation has helped him develop the necessary powers of concentration for Test cricket.

"The one thing I've seen in Emilio is he trains really hard in the nets. He'll bat for ages, putting a lot of hard work in, and it's shown on the pitch," added Tongue.

"Even last week at Lord's, he had two quite horrible dismissals, but I felt today he batted unbelievable on a tricky pitch.

"He was obviously really disappointed with how he got out. It's not a nice feeling, chopping on, but he's put the team in a really good position for tomorrow."

articles.title: 3 Keys for the Browns' defense against the Jaguars in Week 1
articles.summary: Here are three keys for the Cleveland Browns' defense against the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 1.
articles.body:
After a long offseason full of drama and changes, the Cleveland Browns and newly hired head coach Todd Monken will look to make a statement this week against the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week One of the 2026-27 NFL season.

Last year, the Jaguars won the AFC South with an impressive 13-4 regular-season record. The strong showing last season was partly due to the stout offensive play down the stretch, which means the Browns ' defense must be firing on all cylinders this weekend.

Here are the three keys for the Browns defense as they take on the Jaguars on Sunday afternoon.

The Jaguars' offense in year one under head coach Liam Coen took major leaps in 2025, with quarterback Trevor Lawrence as the key facilitator.

Jacksonville averaged 222.3 passing yards per game last season, which ranked 12th across the entire NFL. This year should be no different for the AFC South powerhouse, with Lawrence and the passing game set to take another step with Coen in year two.

With the Jaguars likely focusing on Lawrence to be the catalyst, the Browns' newest additions on the front four must prove themselves in Week One. Sunday marks rising star and newly acquired EDGE Jared Verse's first regular-season contest with the organization, which means defensive coordinator Mike Rutenberg must rely on Verse and his running mates on the defensive line to apply consistent pressure on Lawrence.

Win at the line of scrimmage against the run game

While Jacksonville's passing game thrived last season, the run game was one of the largest issues for the offense.

Averaging the 20th-most rushing yards per game in 2025-26 (115.1 rushing yards per game), the Jaguars tried to revamp the run game this offseason by signing free agent Chris Rodriguez Jr., who spent last season with the Washington Commanders . Both Rodriguez and 2025 fourth-round pick Bhayshul Tuten are set to play a huge role in the run game this year, which means the Browns must take advantage on Sunday.

The return of defensive tackles Mason Graham and Maliek Collins will dramatically help the defense against the run in Week One, with both playmakers poised to be real threats for the Jaguars' run game.

Lawrence's main receiving threat this season has quickly become 2023 sixth-round pick Parker Washington.

The former Penn State standout had a breakout season in 2025, recording 847 receiving yards and five touchdowns on 58 receptions. Coen has been on record this offseason speaking highly of Washington and how he will once again become a key factor on offense this season.

Unfortunately for the Browns, Washington plays a majority of his snaps in the slot, which is one of the weak links on defense heading into the regular season. Cornerback Myles Harden is projected to be the starting nickel for Cleveland in Week One, so the secondary unit will have its hands full with Washington on Sunday.

articles.title: Patriots reach injury settlement with defensive lineman Isaiah Iton
articles.summary: Isaiah Iton reverted to injured reserve at the end of August.
articles.body:
Isaiah Iton will have a chance to continue 2026 on the field.

The New England Patriots waived the defensive tackle from injured reserve with a settlement on Wednesday, according to the NFL transaction wire. He will become a street free agent after going unclaimed.

Iton, 25, had been waived by in Foxborough with an injury designation at the 53-man roster deadline in August. The 6-foot-3, 300-pound defensive lineman subsequently reverted to season-ending injured reserve as the practice squad began to form last week.

Originally entering the NFL as an undrafted free agent in 2024, Iton spent his rookie year on the practice squad of the Tennessee Titans and was briefly retained on a futures contract. From there, the former transfer from Northern Colorado, Hutchinson Community College, Ole Miss and Rutgers attended rookie minicamp at Gillette Stadium as a second-year tryout. A deal followed. Yet so did a 2025 campaign on injured reserve.

After not being tendered as an exclusive rights free agent in March, Iton ultimately circled back to the Patriots heading into training camp in July. He handled five tackles and one quarterback hurry in preseason action last month, staying in for 77 defensive snaps.

With a settlement now reached, six players remain on injured reserve for the reigning AFC champions.

The group includes running back Myles Montgomery, tight end Julian Hill and wide receiver Jeremiah Webb , while offensive tackle Marcus Bryant , linebacker Khalil Jacobs and punter Bryce Baringer are all eligible for activation after missing four games.

The Seattle Seahawks host Wednesday's season opener at Lumen Field. Kickoff is set for 8:20 p.m. ET.

articles.summary: New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh quickly dismissed speculation surrounding wide receiver Malik Nabers after he left practice early on Wednesday. He...
articles.body:
New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh quickly dismissed speculation surrounding wide receiver Malik Nabers after he left practice early on Wednesday. He confirmed to The Athletic's Dan Duggan that post-practice medical checks revealed no injury concerns following the star pass-catcher's extensive recovery from a torn ACL sustained in 2025.

This clean bill of health brings the most encouraging news New York fans have received all summer. With a crucial NFC East season opener against the Dallas Cowboys approaching, the Giants benefited from significant developments regarding their primary offensive weapon during their first official regular-season practice.

Breaking the game-week milestone on X, NFL insider Ari Meirov confirmed that Nabers is operating without any physical restrictions : "Good news: #Giants WR Malik Nabers , returning from a torn ACL, was a full participant in practice today — the team's first official practice of the 2026 regular season, per HC John Harbaugh. The Giants host the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday Night."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Nabers' full participation confirms that he has cleared every physical hurdle after tearing his ACL and meniscus early last season. Rejoining 11-on-11 drills at full speed provides an immediate boost of explosiveness to an offense looking for dynamic perimeter playmakers. With the Cowboys traveling to MetLife Stadium for Sunday Night Football, having a healthy Nabers capable of stretching defenses completely alters New York's offensive game plan.

His rapid progression also highlights New York's careful summer timeline. When Nabers was held out of joint training camp sessions against the Miami Dolphins in August , ESPN's Jordan Raanan reported that this was a planned precaution by Harbaugh to protect the star receiver in potentially risky scrimmage settings. This measured approach has paid off, positioning Nabers at peak strength just as the regular season begins.

articles.title: Paulo Costa the latest addition to Eddie Hearn's representation
articles.summary: Paulo Costa joins the growing list of UFC fighters to be represented by Eddie Hearn.
articles.body:
Eddie Hearn continues his purge of the UFC roster, with Paulo Costa the latest to sign under the Brit.

Hearn's Matchroom Talent Agency is an athlete and entertainment management company that provides promising fighters with better representation. Historically, Matchroom Sport has operated as a promotional powerhouse, but has since had a change of heart and opened up a talent management division earlier this year.

Following the acquisition of Tom Aspinall and Ian Machado Garry , Eddie Hearn has sought out Paulo Costa, who claimed to be the latest to join the growing team.

"I had a great meeting with Eddie Hearn; he's a great guy," Costa said. "I'm so excited to work with him. He already sent us a contract. So, yep. We have a contract. Eddie just sent us a contract already, so I'm so excited. I think we're going to do great things together. Great things."

When asked whether Hearn would be representing and managing him, Paulo Costa confirmed the news.

"He sent me [a contract] a couple days ago… Both [representing and managing]. The whole thing. I have so much respect for what he's doing. He's a great guy. A great professional. I think we're going to do great things together."

"I just need to send back the email. We have this, and I think everything's set up, and I'm so excited."

Being a prominent contender in both the middleweight and light heavyweight divisions, Costa could have had his pick of representation. Ultimately, he chose Eddie Hearn for the quality he brings to the sport .

"He knows the business. He handles business very well. He's a super important person in the fight business. Not only boxing, but he's coming to MMA right now. I think this is a great acquisition for the MMA community."

articles.title: Cameron Jordan will miss the third game of his 15-year Saints career
articles.summary: This is a big loss. Cameron Jordan has been ruled out for Week 1, meaning he'll miss just the third game of his 15-year New Orleans Saints career.
articles.body:
This is a big loss. Cameron Jordan has already been ruled out for Week 1, meaning he'll miss just the third game of his 15-year New Orleans Saints career. Saints coach Kellen Moore announced the decision to sideline Jordan for what may be the first game of his final season after he suffered a hamstring injury during training camp.

"Cam Jordan did not practice with a hamstring. Cam will not play this week," Moore said in his introductory statement . Moore was asked if he had ever felt it was possible Jordan could have played in the Sept. 13 season opener, responding, "Cam's going to do everything possible to play in this game. He's progressing well, he's done a really good job during this recovery process, and we'll just take it week by week."

When asked if the decision to keep Jordan from going on injured reserve meant the Saints believed he could return before Week 4, Moore answered: "There's potential. We'll see how this thing responds."

Jordan last practiced on Aug. 6, and while there was the threat of this hamstring issue lingering into Week 1, there was more optimism that he'd be able to return after resting up for more than a month. That hope wasn't unwarranted. Jordan missed his first game in 2021 due to the NFL's COVID-19 protocol, and then he had to miss another game in 2022 after suffering a broken bone in his face. Including the playoffs, he suited up for 171 consecutive games from 2011 to 2020. It says a lot about his durability that he's still appeared in 243 regular season games and 11 playoff games in his 15-year career. At the same time, he's 37, and the Saints are going to be without one of their three best edge rushers in a pivotal Week 1 kickoff game. Guys like Anfernee Jennings and Tyree Wilson must step up behind Chase Young and Carl Granderson .

articles.title: Malik Nabers has full practice, appears "ready to go" for season opener
articles.summary: Wide receiver Malik Nabers has not played in almost a year, since tearing his right ACL in a Sept. 28 game against the Chargers.
articles.body:
Wide receiver Malik Nabers has not played in almost a year, since tearing his right ACL in a Sept. 28 game against the Chargers. The Giants have been coy about his status for the season opener against the Cowboys, but Nabers was a full participant in Wednesday's padded practice.

"I think he's ready to go , man," coach John Harbaugh said after practice, via video from SNY Giants. "We'll see. It's still four days until we play. If he's ready to go, and he feels like he's ready to go, then he'll play. If he's not ready, then he won't play."

Nabers said Monday he didn't want to come back on a snap count, and it appears he won't be. He caught nine passes for 167 yards and two touchdowns in a Week 2 loss to the Cowboys last season.

Every player on the Giants' 53-man roster practiced.

Tight end Theo Johnson (shoulder), offensive lineman Bryan Hudson (knee), defensive lineman Shelby Harris (Achilles) and offensive tackle Andrew Thomas (knee) were also full participants.

articles.title: Elly De La Cruz's 102 mph relay assist had MLB fans in complete awe
articles.summary: Really might be the most ridiculous throw... ever?
articles.body:
The Reds may be decidedly mediocre, but Elly De La Cruz is far from that. The Red shortstop has the tools to leave a stadium in awe at a given moment. That's exactly what happened on Tuesday night in Los Angeles .

Since Statcast began tracking throws in 2015, no infield player has thrown a baseball harder in an assist than what De La Cruz did at Dodger Stadium.

With the game tied in the third inning and Teoscar Hernández at the plate, the Dodgers outfielder had himself a likely inside-the-park home run after Dane Myers whiffed badly on his diving attempt. The ball rolled all the way to the wall, and left fielder JJ Bleday wasn't even in the frame.

The entire mission was to retrieve the ball and get it to De La Cruz who was some 200 feet away from the plate. It didn't matter that Hernández was rounding third. De La Cruz unleashed a 102 mph throw to get Hernández out with ease. The throw was initially registered at 105.3 mph before Statcast modified it to 102 .

Still, everything about that throw was ridiculous. The break on that ball, the precision — just wow. It also had to help that Hernández's sprinting capacity appeared to be 270 feet. But De La Cruz was likely the lone infielder who could have made that throw.

Fans were beyond impressed, as they should have been.

articles.title: NFHCA Top-10 Talk: Week Two
articles.summary: We’ve got a pulse on where the best are coming from.
articles.body:
Last Week: 4-3 (OT) W vs. No. 6 Duke, 2-0 W at Boston College

This Week: vs. No. 14 Louisville, vs. No. 16 Miami (OH)

Northwestern was back to full strength with Ashley Sessa and Olivia Bent-Cole rejoining the team, but it had to fight for its two wins this weekend in the Big Ten-ACC Challenge. After going down 3-1 at halftime, the 'Cats went back to ol' reliable on the penalty corner: Sessa insert, Bent-Cole stop, Ilse Tromp drag flick for two fourth-quarter scores to send it into overtime.

That's where the new blood sealed the deal: Sol Martinez was left wide open in the center of the circle, and after some vintage Piper Borz stick work, she got the ball right in front of the cage to end it.

BC held NU scoreless through the entire first half, but adversity was quickly overcome in the second in the 2-0 win on Sunday.

With two more ranked opponents to come, NU continues to grow stronger at an exponential rate

Last Week: 9-0 W vs. Lehigh, 8-0 W vs. Ball State

This Week: vs. No. 16 Miami (OH), vs. No. 14 Louisville

The Hawkeyes are THE story of non-conference play. Nobody expected them to tear through their first four contests in the fashion they did, but they've made it abundantly clear that they're coming for a Final Four berth this season.

Dionne van Aalsum already has 14 points through this part of the season and doesn't even lead her own team. That's scary. Fréderique van Cleef — through four games , as a reminder — has amassed over 65% of her points total in 2025, leading the nation with 19. The pair combined for a ridiculous 11 goals this weekend, both games being multi-goal efforts from each.

Van Aalsum and van Cleef are a scary 1-2 punch for Iowa to weaponize. They are one of two duos to rank in the nation's top 10 in goals (Clara Larripa and Abril Peroni, Richmond). The difference is that they occupy two of the country's top three spots. Their upcoming slate, nearly identical to Northwestern's, will give us a strong pulse as to how Iowa will measure up in Big Ten play.

Last Week: 5-1 W vs. UMass Lowell, 1-0 W vs. No. 9 UConn

This Week: vs. No. 12 UMass, vs. Boston College

You should be catching on to a pattern here: the best teams in the nation get tested early. Northwestern got its test against Duke, Iowa got its test against North Carolina and the Crimson got theirs against a hungry UConn team seeking revenge after a heartbreaking loss to Harvard in the NCAA Quarterfinals.

For nearly 50 minutes, you felt an upset brewing in this matchup. Then, the Huskies gave up one too many penalty corners, and that was that.

Sometimes when you're in a stalemate, you need to take what you can get. No need to overcomplicate things. That's why Harvard came out the victor on Sunday.

Much like the two teams ahead of them, the Crimson are extremely well-rounded: five total goal scorers and nine point-getters this past weekend, while Linde Burger saved six of seven shots on goal.

Last Week: 4-0 W vs. Old Dominion, 0-1 (2-3 SO) L at No. 1o North Carolina

This Week: vs. No. 17 Rutgers, at Penn State

The absence of defense was what cost the Tigers a national championship. Against UNC, it was the complete opposite: the absence of late offense. In 75 minutes, Princeton only logged six shots on target and kept the Tar Heels around for too long.

With that said, this loss is extremely uncharacteristic for the 2025 national runner-up, and when it's put into perspective, it makes much more sense. The Tigers were tasked with a motivated North Carolina squad that had dropped its first two contests in Winston-Salem and was red hot after a shellacking of Penn just two days previous. It'd be unfair to hit the panic button on them this early in the season, especially when they're searching for the answers of their identity in the post-Beth Yeager era.

Rutgers presents a solid challenge for Princeton this weekend and a prime opportunity to start solidifying its offense for the higher-ranked teams it has down the road.

Last Week: 7-0 W vs. Penn, 1-0 (3-2 SO) W vs. No. 2 Princeton

This Week: vs. No. 2o Old Dominion, at Richmond

What a bounce-back weekend for North Carolina.

Question marks began to arise about who the Tar Heels would be in year four of the Erin Matson era two weekends ago. Every last one of them was put to bed.

The gates to Karen Shelton Stadium were completely blown off on Friday, and at the front of the charge was an unexpected face out of the midfield: first-year midfielder Sofia Ferri — the ACC Offensive Player of the Week who put away the first brace of her career, the precursor to her game-winning score to beat Princeton in Sunday's shootout.

Merritt Skubisz completed UNC's first sweep of the ACC weekly honors, claiming Defensive Player of the Week after making six saves in her 150 minutes in the cage. After splitting time with Katie Wimmer a season ago, Skubisz is in a battle with graduate student Tessa Shahbo for the starting job in 2026, and she's bolstered her resume with a career performance against the national runner-up.

Ferri only trails Charly Bruder for the team points lead, as the pair stands as the only Tar Heels to log multiple goals on the young season. UNC has a two-way forward with superstar potential in its lap, and it could carry it far into the 2026 postseason.

Not much from Wake Forest last week, as it ended up being one of the few teams in the top 20 with one game on the slate. But the Deacs did the most with what they had, as they went to five different players on the attack for their six scores on Friday. The most jarring thing on the stat sheet was Wake's 22 shots on goal, its most since Oct. 10 of last year.

Even knowing this kind of mind-blowing statistic, the most impressive nugget from this game might be the zero shots taken by Ohio in the second half. The defense has started to saddle up after allowing Iowa to climb into the double digits in the shots category, and it's begun to pay off in the polls.

Last Week: 2-0 W at Boston College, 3-2 (3-1 SO) W vs. No. 6 Duke

This Week: vs. Towson, vs. Saint Joseph's

Say hello to this week's biggest climbers: the Terps.

Maryland hasn't climbed this high since last season's preseason poll, so this is quite the shake-up and makes the complexion of the top 10 extremely intriguing. It's also reinvigorated the Big Ten-ACC field hockey rivalry, as the former has a legitimate case for being the best field hockey conference in the nation with four teams in the top 10, the most among any conference.

The Terrapins also ensured a B1G sweep in Newton this past weekend with their two victories, a major resume boost.

Their victory over Duke was much more impressive than the stat sheet shows — they displayed true resolve after getting punched in the mouth to start, going down 2-0 after the first quarter. After cutting the lead in half a few moments later, they wouldn't find the equalizer for another 40 minutes and change.

They kept hammering away though and eventually got one of their four fourth-quarter shots to clank off the boards and force overtime. It was wraps from there. A signature win.

Last Week: 4-0 W vs. Kent State, 4-1 W vs. Vermont

The Wolverines did what they were supposed to do at home: dominate. A weekend highlighted by an Esmée de Willigen hat trick brought Big Blue opportunities to fiddle with the lineups they put out.

The most important thing to note on U-M as of now is their strength of schedule. Michigan doesn't play a ranked opponent until next month, when it faces Iowa, Northwestern and Maryland all in succession to open up their friendly confines to conference play. The wins could start tallying up in the near future, but the big question is: will the Wolverines be ready?

Last Week: 3-4 (OT) L vs. No. 1 Northwestern, 2-3 (1-3 SO) L vs. No. 13 Maryland

This past weekend was a rough one for the Blue Devils — absolute chaos. Nobody can really knock them for the valiant efforts they put up against the Big Ten. In theory, when you fire off 18 shots against anyone, you'd assume more than two find the back of the cage.

Ashley Stockdale looks like the talent that the entire nation thought she'd be with five goals through the start of the season. As a unit, however, there's work to be done. Duke's averaging 3.25 goals per game, good for 15th-best nationally, but ACC foes Cal and Wake Forest have been on fire as of late. If we're in for an Atlantic Coast shootout this fall, Duke may be one of the few powerhouses left on the outside looking in on the NCAA Tournament if it doesn't get the job done in the conference tournament.

Last Week: 3-0 W at Brown, 0-1 L at No. 3 Harvard

This Week: at No. 17 Rutgers, vs. Villanova

The Huskies entered the weekend seeking to make a statement against the squad that dispatched them in the postseason last year, but came away with the same agonizing pain of defeat they felt last November.

UConn seems like the bridesmaid right now, just one elite victory away from breaking into the upper echelon of the sport. With seven different goal scorers through the first four games of the season, the attack seems as dynamic as a Huskies fan would like it to be. Princeton's on the horizon, just 11 days away. Maybe that brings their breakthrough into top-five consideration.

articles.title: Yankees place Jazz Chisholm Jr. on IL with sprained thumb
articles.summary: The Yankees place Jazz Chisholm Jr. on the IL; will they bring back Anthony Volpe?
articles.body:
Jazz Chisholm Jr. is reportedly joining the 10-day injured list with a sprained right thumb. Another injury to add to the Yankees' extensive list this season.

MLB Insider Bryan Hoch reported the news on Wednesday, revealing that Chisholm is unable to participate in baseball activities for 7-10 days. Manager Aaron Boone indicated within the last hour that they just heard the news, so a replacement might not be available to join the team tonight. All told, not what you want to hear in the heart of September baseball and just days away from the Subway Series, but on the other hand, a new space in the roster could be the perfect shuffle the Pinstripes need to finally gain a consistent momentum.

The Yankees have several options to call up and add depth to the roster. Fans probably have mixed feelings on this subject, but placing Chisholm on the IL also opens the possibility of Anthony Volpe 's return to the majors. Reports confirmed that Boone would be "comfortable" with putting the New Jersey native at 2B. Max Schuemann and Oswaldo Cabrera are both already on the 40-man roster as well and could be options if the Yankees want someone in more of a bench role.

Following through with Volpe could be the spark needed for this offense to propel into the postseason. He's been especially hot of late with a .440 average and a .533 OBP for the Scranton/Wilkes-Barre RailRiders in September. He'll be a huge asset in the Bronx if he can maintain or bolster his numbers, but it would make sense to be cautiously optimistic at this point.

Chisholm will likely rejoin the lineup once he's reinstated from the IL, which could be just in time for arguably one of the most crucial series against the Rays .
